messages:
alex: Quick sync — drafting rollout spec for the feature-flagged model switch. Need decisions on pin strategy, experiment windows, and rollback triggers.
mira: Can we keep customer pinning for 90 days after rollout? some customers asked to lock until they validate outputs.
sam: 90 days sounds long. Can we do 30 days default, with opt-in 90 via account settings?
ajex: (typo) alex: agree with sam, default 30 + opt-in 90. Need acceptance criteria for experiment success though.
deb: Proposed success metrics: error rate (5xx), median 95th latency (ms), and quality regression on eval prompts (delta <= 1% fuzz/score).
mira: Also add business metric: downstream click-through or conversion delta within +/-2% for top 10 customers in cohort.
sam: For rollbacks: immediate rollback if 5xx spike > 0.5% absolute or p95 latency regression > 200ms sustained for 10 minutes. Manual abort option for SEs too.
jen: What about gradual percentages? I suggest: 1% -> 5% -> 25% -> 100%, each stage 30m stability check, except first stage 10m.
alex: Sounds good. Add automated gating: deploy-bot will monitor health signals and auto-block promotion on threshold breach.
deploy-bot: NOTE: automatic promotion can be disabled per-release by adding "auto_promote: false" to rollout config.
mira: We need pinned-version behavior: customers who pin should always route to their pinned version even during experiment. Pinned users excluded from experiment buckets.
sam: Agree. For pinned users, provide a migration path: a 'preview' toggle to test new version against pinned in a shadow mode for 48h.
deb: Acceptance criteria (draft): 1) No quality regression >1% on eval suite. 2) No increase in 5xx >0.2% absolute. 3) p95 latency delta <150ms. 4) No critical customer complaint within 48h for pinned customers.
jen: Edge cases: regional capacity degradation — need fallback to nearest compatible model variant or region. Document that fallback may change latency and we should mark users affected in logs.
alex: Also call out experiment overlap: prevent two major model rollouts overlapping on same customer segment. We should block promotions if active rollout tag conflicts.
mira: For experiment design, who owns sample allocation? product owns buckets but infra enforces isolation and sticky hashing.
sam: Add technical detail: sticky hash is user_id mod 100; rollout percentages map to ranges. Ex: 0-0 => 1%, 0-4 => 5%, etc.
jen: I'll paste a quick config snippet for the rollout manifest:
```yaml
release: model-v2.3.1
buckets:
  - percent: 1
    range: 0-0
  - percent: 5
    range: 1-4
  - percent: 20
    range: 5-24
pins_excluded: true
auto_promote: true
health_checks:
  error_rate_threshold: 0.005
  p95_latency_delta_ms: 200
  evaluation_regression_pct: 1.0
```
mira: Nice. Also require a canary note in the changelog with sample prompts and expected behavior for SRE/Support.
deb: Logging/observability: we need per-route telemetry for quality signals (prompt family), token counts, and model variant tag. Also sample logging of inputs for postmortem (masked PII).
sam: Rollback plan: immediate rollback to model-v2.3.0, preserve KV caches where possible, and invalidate caches if regression persists. Run a post-rollback diagnosis job that compares top 100 failing prompts.
alex: Who signs off for GA? PM + Infra + SRE + Trust. Also product ops must confirm canary dashboards are green for 24h at 100%.
mira: For customer-driven asks: build a self-serve 'pin expiration' feature so customers can set an expiration at pin time.
jen: I'll write the PRD section for rollout and include these acceptance criteria + config example. Posting draft in #prds later.
alex: Thanks — next actions: jen to draft PRD; deb to list telemetry dashboards; sam to add gating logic to rollout service; mira to scope pin-expiration UI. We'll reconvene tomorrow. :thumbsup:
